QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_40

question.text: Under the AB Responsible Services IWMP, 76% water availability increased in project villages. The SIA's BEST approach to verify is:

answer.text: Compare to national average water availability
Check groundwater-level data pre/post (state groundwater board), household water-consumption metered data, and physical inspection of check-dams + rainfall-normalised comparison

explanation.text: The Logic: SAS-500 water-availability verification needs: (i) groundwater board data (administrative), (ii) metered household consumption (primary), (iii) structure inspection (physical), (iv) RAINFALL NORMALISATION to avoid attributing good-monsoon year to the intervention. The Trap: Option A abandons scepticism. Option C is single-source verbal. Option B is benchmarking, not verification. Cross-Exam Context: Similar multi-source verification logic in III-A / III-C Compliance and XV Research Analyst. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Always rainfall-normalise water-intervention outcomes — monsoon variability can easily explain a 70% swing. Ask for IMD district rainfall data for the project period and baseline year.
